edition.note: Open Library: Crown Business, September 13, 2011, ISBN 9780307887894; the work record lists no revised edition, only reprints and translations. The copyright page in the opened text reads "Copyright © 2011 by Eric Ries ... Crown Business" with CIP data "1st ed." The Lessons use chapters 1 to 9 of that edition; nothing rests on later material.

rows.claim: Part One, Vision, is chapters 1 to 4.
rows.note: Read in a full-text copy of the book that is not an authorised source, so it is not linked; the link is the catalogue entry for the book. Contents page of the text: "Part One VISION 1. Start 2. Define 3. Learn 4. Experiment". The text is a reader-uploaded copy on the Internet Archive, not a publisher page; theleanstartup.com/book confirms the three part names Vision, Steer, Accelerate.

rows.claim: Chapters 5 and 6 are Leap and Test and hold the Build-Measure-Learn loop and the MVP.
rows.note: Read in a full-text copy of the book that is not an authorised source, so it is not linked; the link is the catalogue entry for the book. Contents: "Part Two STEER 5. Leap 6. Test 7. Measure 8. Pivot (or Persevere)". The loop diagram and "Minimize TOTAL time through the loop" open Part Two.

rows.claim: Drew Houston made a short video before the product was ready; the beta waiting list jumped from 5,000 to 75,000 people overnight.
rows.note: Ries's own excerpt of the book on TechCrunch quotes Houston: "Our beta waiting list went from 5,000 people to 75,000 people literally overnight." The video is "a simple three-minute demonstration of the technology as it is meant to work". The figure is Houston's account, as the book gives it.

rows.claim: Chapters 7 to 9 are Measure, Pivot (or Persevere) and Batch.
rows.note: Read in a full-text copy of the book that is not an authorised source, so it is not linked; the link is the catalogue entry for the book. Contents: "7. Measure 8. Pivot (or Persevere) Part Three ACCELERATE 9. Batch". Batch opens Part Three, so the Lesson spans two parts; the chapter numbers and titles are right.

rows.claim: IMVU released code to production as often as fifty times a day.
rows.note: Read in a full-text copy of the book that is not an authorised source, so it is not linked; the link is the catalogue entry for the book. Not listed; open item from the earlier audit. Chapter 9 reads: "IMVU makes about fifty changes to its product (on average) every single day." "As often as fifty" made the average a ceiling. Card now says about fifty changes on average every day, in both languages. Ries's blog (https://www.startuplessonslearned.com/2009/06/why-continuous-deployment.html) says "as often as an average of fifty times a day". Check b20c1l3k5 needed no change.
